bio:
I'm a perception software engineer at Lucid Motors, where I work on the real-time LiDAR and ultrasonic sensor fusion and occupancy mapping that runs on our production vehicles. Most of my work is in C++ and Python, across perception, sensor fusion, SLAM and motion planning, and I've used ROS and ROS2 on autonomous mobile robots and multi-robot systems.

I did my Master's in Robotics Engineering at Worcester Polytechnic Institute, where I focused on SLAM, path planning and robot perception. Before Lucid, I wrote multi-arm welding software for Path Robotics, worked on robotics software quality for Berkshire Grey, and built outdoor localization for an AMR at Void Robotics by fusing RTK GPS, visual odometry and an IMU. Before grad school, I spent several years building machine vision and automation systems at Nagarro Software and Automation Systems and Solution.
